title: Sticky until saturated: token-aware routing
gist: The open Kubernetes inference router replaced a four-signal blend with one cache-affinity filter plus one load signal chosen to match the workload's bottleneck: uncached tokens in flight when prefill-bound, active streams when decode-bound. Stickiness lets go at a saturation limit calibrated per deployment.
changes: An unusually candid like-for-like measurement of workload-aware routing: large where prefill dominates, nothing where decode does. The calibration does not transfer between models, chips or engines, a small concrete case of the optimum being specific to the deployment.
caveats: Each point was run once. The baseline is round-robin, a weak one. The authors say a hand-tuned weight set can still beat their default on the workload it was tuned for.

bears_on.note: The right load signal depends on whether the workload is prefill-bound or decode-bound.
The per-deployment part is one calibrated threshold, not a bespoke stack.
